**Performance: block** at `a7a0f4a470532ae54d0103528b2bf338abff3bfe`.

Full PR-owned cost review against main `cee011387937c7881318c98d86014526d94f2ca7`, source plus exact-head CI only. Candidate gating and the once-per-stretch behavior have meaningful tests. The requested **capture without a tmux process** is not guaranteed.

## P156-F001: modal capture inherits a fork/reconnect path

`daemon/src/modal_stall.rs:65` calls the generic `TmuxPort::capture`. Production `tmux/src/lib.rs:1133-1142` delegates to `stdout`; `stdout:471-477` uses the control answer if available, otherwise calls `run`, which records **`tmux.capture-pane` and launches an executable** (`352-358`).

`control.rs:229-281` returns None on failed start, reconnect backoff, failed send or a three-second reply timeout. It can also start a new **`tmux.control-client`** when no live client exists (`297-312`). Therefore newly recurring modal captures can activate existing launch sites. With C silent candidates, a failed control service can cause **C fallback captures per watchdog round**, roughly C/60 launches/s at a 60-second cadence, plus connection attempts/replacements. Calling an existing site does not make its newly exercised work zero.

This is independently consistent with passing CI cases **`a_lost_control_client_falls_back_then_reconnects`** and **`a_stalled_control_client_is_killed_and_replaced`**. The separate **`reads_after_warm_up_launch_no_tmux_process`** case proves healthy warmed reuse, not the failed-client path.

The PR body honestly says a forked capture occurs while control is down. The PM packet, AC2 and the non-goal require no tmux process; the plan/backpressure still describe a zero-launch read. **These are different budgets.**

**Required disposition:** either give this detector a control-only capture that reports unavailability and defers the candidate without starting/forking clients, preserving other callers' fallback behavior; or explicitly accept/document the recovery exception and its rate/latency budget. Proof must exercise the detector with a failed/unavailable control client and verify whichever contract is accepted, not only FakeTmux calls or warmed control reuse.

## Steady-state and per-seat cost

Let N be listed seats, W live-by-record working/paned Copilot or Claude seats, C those silent at least 20 minutes by their own events, and M retained modal-stall rows.

| Surface | Actual work |
|---|---|
| Scheduling | Added to the existing PA watchdog round, before its PA-specific processing. No new independent timer/task loop. Work is sequential, so captures and notification waits add to that round's latency. |
| Healthy seat | One `Spine::latest_matching` **API call per W seat per round**, not one SQL SELECT. `store/src/spine.rs:317-344` performs a schema check, opens a read snapshot, makes **four indexed per-kind SELECTs** on `(seat,kind,seq)`, decodes up to four full event rows, then rolls back the snapshot. At 60 s, that is about **0.067 indexed SELECTs/s per eligible seat**, plus schema/transaction overhead. It does not scan each seat's whole history. Payload bytes also matter. |
| Candidate gating | O(N) filter over seats already listed. Idle, paneless, tombstoned, OMP and Pi rows skip the silence query. A supported working seat without an own event still pays the query but never captures. A recent-own-event seat pays the query and no capture. Thus **zero pane reads with no candidate is true; zero added reads with healthy working seats is false**. |
| Capturing | Exactly one port capture per C candidate per round, including silent candidates whose screen is normal and matches nothing. Healthy control reuse makes no process per capture. Recovery exceptions are F001. The generic capture obtains the entire visible pane and only then keeps up to 500 physical rows; 500 is not a pre-read byte limit. |
| Matching | Builds a vector of nonblank borrowed rows and checks the fixed three-marker table. Linear in captured screen bytes/rows with fixed marker count; no model call or shell command. The first line is capped at 160 Unicode characters, at most 640 UTF-8 bytes, not necessarily 160 bytes. |
| Stored inventory | The first successful candidate capture loads **all M latest-per-seat stall rows**, even if no modal matches. One successful read per round; on a read failure later candidates retry it. Each candidate linearly searches that vector: **O(M + C*M)** work plus string/payload allocation. M includes old/tombstoned seats; no pruning/hard inventory cap is added. |
| Writes and telling | A new stretch makes one schema-checked owned UPSERT transaction before notifications. Unchanged known stretches make no new claim or message; a disappearing/reappearing dialog can make an open-state UPDATE transaction. At most two distinct recipients are told per newly claimed stretch. Scope/target selection reuses roster walks, PA ancestry and repository placement. |
| Notification cost | First/repeated failed placement of an uncached folder can call existing **`git.pa-watchdog-common-dir`**; negative placement is not cached in this base. Normal parent/PA wakes can invoke existing delivery/queue, cold-wake audit and model work, with inherited transport launches where applicable. One modal audit publication is also attempted. This is not a globally flat-spawn or zero-inference-cost workflow. |
| Views | Each `/v1/seats` request adds a standing-stalls query and O(local roster size * returned standing stalls) matching. Each named `/v1/state` adds a standing-stalls query too. The global inventory has no open-row index; the own-event anti-join uses the existing `(seat,kind,at,seq)` index. The optional `?1 IS NULL OR m.seat=?1` predicate has no new query-plan proof of a named-seat seek. Returned cardinality does not prove bounded underlying table work. |

The new module's healthy-seat comment acknowledges an indexed read; the plan AC1/AC5 and backpressure still claim healthy seats cost nothing extra/zero added reads. Update those claims to the actual bounded-but-nonzero database budget, including the four per-kind seeks.

Captures use synchronous control waits inside the async round. A lost client can consume its three-second timeout before fallback, and the generic forked `Command::output` has no detector-specific timeout. A sequence of bad captures can delay other watchdog work. No local timing claim is made here.

## Proof and limits

[CI 42381309337](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42381309337) succeeds in all four jobs; both visible delivers checks succeed, latest **42381667195**. This exact head is CLEAN. JUnit records **2,089 executed cases, zero failures**, with five Rust tests skipped separately.

Executed cases include candidate thresholds and exclusions; real-screen matcher positives and working/quoted-text negatives; the real-store candidate/notification tests; restart/re-arm and once-only store behavior; HTTP views; and all six spawn guards. The positive FakeTmux capture counts demonstrate the counting instrument works: under-20-minute/recent/OMP rows get zero while the silent normal-screen candidate gets three across three rounds, and a claimed dialog gets four across repeat/restart rounds with one message per target.

Those modal tests use a **FakeTmux**, real registry/spine/queue and local HTTP router. They do not prove the production capture's zero-launch recovery path. Existing real-tmux CI supplies the contrary fallback behavior and the narrower healthy-reuse proof. No local builds, tests, probes, live captures, daemon restarts, model calls or worktree changes.

Migration 0040 and schema 40 are above this main's 36 and the currently proposed 0038/0039. Merge-order numbering still applies if another migration moves main first.

**After deployment, once F001's budget is resolved:** measure same-PID/build site deltas for `tmux.capture-pane`, `tmux.control-client`, scope Git and downstream delivery separately; control capture count versus W/C and actual round elapsed time; daemon CPU/RSS; modal inventory/query extent and view request rates. Include healthy non-candidates and independently evidenced legitimate candidates. Zero captures alone says nothing about the four-per-kind silence reads. No live reading is claimed; it remains owed.
